title: VocabularyImport
description: Array of words importable into one vocabulary. The vocabulary decides the words' language; translations are keyed by language code (de, en, fa). Import the same "id" again to update a word. Store only what is listed here: the app works out every other form when it shows the word (German noun cases and all tenses; English plurals and all tenses).

id.description: Optional stable id, e.g. 'b1-noun-abend'. Re-importing a word with the same id updates it instead of adding a duplicate.

headword.description: The word itself, without article, e.g. 'Abend', 'anfangen', 'sich amüsieren', 'give up'. A leading 'to' on an English verb is ignored.

translations.description: Translations keyed by language code; at least one language other than the vocabulary's own.

nounForms.description: Optional. German nouns need 'article' for their case tables and 'plural' for their plural tables. An English noun without a stored plural gets a derived one.

article.description: German only: der, die or das. Ignored in languages without articles.

plural.description: Dictionary notation or the full word: '-e' (Tag → Tage), '-s', '-' (unchanged), '¨-er' (Haus → Häuser), '¨' (Apfel → Äpfel), 'Kinder', 'cacti'. Null: no plural.

verbForms.description: Principal parts the other forms are derived from. Required for German verbs (leave a part out and the tenses built on it are not shown). Optional in English, where missing parts are derived and stored parts win, e.g. { "simplePast": "dreamt", "perfect": "dreamt" }.

infinitive.description: Defaults to the headword, e.g. 'anfangen', 'sich amüsieren'.

presentThirdPerson.description: e.g. 'fängt an', 'amüsiert sich', 'goes'. German: the vowel change and a separable prefix are read from this.

perfect.description: With or without the auxiliary: 'hat angefangen', 'ist gefahren', 'gone'.

passive.description: e.g. 'wird gemacht', 'is written'. Any value turns on the passive tables, which are built from the past participle; null or absent means the verb has none.

auxiliaryIsSein.description: German: use 'sein' in the perfect tenses. Also read from a 'perfect' starting with 'ist'.

text.description: The sentence in the vocabulary's language

german.description: Older alias of 'text', still accepted on import.

regionalVariant.description: Optional, e.g. 'CH' or 'A' for Swiss/Austrian standard variants.
